papers.title: Discovery of the β-Carboline Biosynthetic Pathway Enables In Planta Reconstruction of the Amazonian Brew Ayahuasca
papers.abstract: {beta}-Carbolines are bioactive indole alkaloids with remarkable pharmacological properties and a defining role in ayahuasca, a traditional Amazonian shamanic brew, where their inhibition of monoamine oxidases enables the oral activity of the psychoactive N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT). Yet, despite their longstanding medicinal and cultural significance, the biosynthetic origin of {beta}-carbolines in plants remains largely unresolved. Here, we uncover key steps underlying the biosynthesis of harmine, the major bioactive {beta}-carboline alkaloid in Peganum harmala, by integrating spatial metabolite and transcriptome profiling with enzyme characterization and pathway reconstruction. We discovered four enzymes that enable de novo harmine biosynthesis in Nicotiana benthamiana and revealed how two closely related cytochrome P450s exhibit divergent regioselectivity, directing tryptamine towards either {beta}-carboline or serotonin biosynthesis. Structural modeling and targeted mutagenesis pinpoint active-site residues that switch this regioselectivity, revealing a molecular basis for diversification of tryptamine metabolism. By combining distinct tryptamine pathways, we achieved de novo co-production of {beta}-carbolines and DMT in N. benthamiana and P. harmala hairy roots without supplementing exogenous precursors. Together, these findings unlock {beta}-carboline biosynthesis for future sustainable bioproduction with broad opportunities spanning medicine, crop protection, and biodiversity conservation.

papers.title: Branched-Chain α-Keto Acid Mitochondrial Uptake Regulates Fatty Acid Metabolism in Adipose Tissue
papers.abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) are essential amino acids and their homeostasis is tightly regulated by mostly mitochondrial localized catabolic activities where branched-chain -keto acids (BCKAs) are the first-step downstream products. BCAAs and BCKAs are both readily detected in circulation, necessitating targeted transporters for their uptake across cellular and mitochondrial membranes. Although mitochondrial transporter for BCAA uptake has been identified, the molecular entity for BCKAs mitochondrial uptake remains unknown. In adult mice, we measured circulating BCAA and BCKAs under feeding and fasting status, and found circulating BCKAs were markedly elevated during fasting while BCAAs levels remained constant. By integrating genetic association analysis in human and multi-tissue nutrient-responsive transcriptomic profiling in mice, we identified SLC25A35 as a candidate mitochondrial transporter highly associated with BCKA homeostasis. SLC25A35 expression was highly enriched in brown adipocytes. Genetic inactivation of SLC25A35 in mice specifically blunted BCKA mitochondria uptake and downstream catabolism without significant impact on BCAA homeostasis, as demonstrated by targeted metabolic profiling and isotope tracing in intact animals, in isolated primary adipocytes and in purified mitochondria. SLC25A35 expression directly promoted mitochondrial BCKA uptake, with a preference for KIC and KMV over KIV. Importantly, SLC25A35 mediated BCKA uptake and catabolism was independent from SLC25A44 mediated BCAA mitochondrial transport, and the BCKA specificity for SLC35A35 was further evaluated by structure-guided identification and mutagenesis based validation for conserved potential BCKA interacting residues in SLC25A35 transmembrane domains. Functionally, SLC25A35 expression enhanced lipogenesis by supporting fatty acid incorporation of BCKA-derived carbon and lipogenic gene expression, independent from mitochondrial production of PEP. During cold exposure, SLC25A35-deficient mice exhibited reduced mitochondrial respiratory activity in brown adipose tissue , depletion of short- and long-chain acylcarnitine species, and attenuated cold-responsive metabolic signalling. Together, these findings identify SLC25A35 as a nutrient-responsive mitochondrial BCKA transporter that reveal a previously unrecognized BCKA specific contribution to adipocyte lipid metabolism and thermogenic adaptation.

papers.title: MUC4 regulatory-region methylation is remodeled during breast cancer progression and metastasis
papers.abstract: Background Mucin-4 (MUC4) contributes to tumor cell survival and metastatic behavior, but its expression in breast cancer is unusual; previous studies have demonstrated that MUC4 levels are reduced in primary tumors relative to normal epithelium but are partially restored in metastatic lesions. Because DNA methylation is known to regulate MUC4 gene expression in cultured cancer cells, we investigated whether methylation of the MUC4 regulatory region changes across breast cancer progression. Results Analysis of the TCGA-BRCA database revealed that primary breast tumors exhibit increased methylation at CpG sites within the MUC4 regulatory region relative to normal breast tissue, and methylation at key sites is inversely associated with MUC4 transcript abundance. Moreover, DNA methyltransferase inhibition with 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine alters MUC4 expression in several breast cancer cell lines. Finally, targeted bisulfite sequencing analysis of an independent cohort of normal breast, primary breast tumor, and metastatic breast cancer specimens revealed that MUC4 in primary tumors is significantly more methylated than in normal breast tissue at all 11 CpG sites examined. Metastatic specimens in this cohort generally display lower methylation than primary tumors and an intermediate methylation profile between normal and primary tissue. Conclusions Taken together, our findings support MUC4 regulatory region methylation as a contributor to stage-dependent MUC4 regulation.

papers.title: YAP1-induced super-enhancer rewiring mediates gene-environment-driven malignant reprogramming and metastatic ecosystem formation in head and neck cancer
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by frequent TP53 mutations, which are insufficient for tumorigenesis and largely undruggable, underscoring the need to define epigenetic mechanisms driving cancer evolution. Here we show that TP53 mutation facilitates YAP1-dependent transcriptional reprogramming, driving epigenetic tumor evolution by hijacking tissue-regenerative programs. Integrated multi-omics analyses of mouse models and multiregional human HNSCC samples reveal that global chromatin architecture remains largely stable during progression, whereas YAP1 dynamically redistributes to newly formed super-enhancers accompanied by enhancer DNA hypomethylation. Mechanistically, YAP1 establishes an IL6-dependent feedforward loop and cooperates with stage-specific transcription factors, including FOXM1, DeltaNp63, and PITX2. The YAP1-PITX2 axis promotes partial EMT, cancer-associated fibroblast activation, and lymph node metastasis, resulting in a fibrotic and immunosuppressive metastatic ecosystem. These findings identify a YAP1-driven epigenetic circuit as a central hub linking environmental stress to malignant reprogramming and highlight a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.

papers.title: Saruparib recapitulates PARP-BRCA synthetic lethality with PARP1-trapping properties limiting its cytotoxicity
papers.abstract: The original concept of PARP synthetic lethality proposes that loss of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) activity selectively kills homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cells. However, clinically approved PARP1/2 inhibitors (PARPis) are used at exposures exceeding those required for catalytic inhibition. At these doses, PARP trapping is cytotoxic to HR-proficient cells and limits the therapeutic window in HR-deficient cancers. Saruparib has been developed as a PARP1-selective inhibitor to reduce PARP2-associated toxicity; yet its PARP1-trapping properties remain incompletely characterized. Here, we show that saruparib exhibits trapping properties distinct from those of conventional PARPis. It causes minimal cytotoxicity in HR-proficient cells and remains minimally toxic in XRCC1-deficient cells, which are highly sensitive to trapping-associated cytotoxicity induced by conventional PARPis. Although methyl methanesulfonate, which induces extensive base damage, increases saruparib-induced PARP1 trapping and cytotoxicity, the overall trapping-associated cytotoxic response is weaker than that induced by olaparib and shows little further dose-dependent increase once catalytic PARP1 inhibition is achieved. Biochemical measurements demonstrated that PARP1-DNA complexes formed in the presence of saruparib are less stable than those in the presence of olaparib or talazoparib. Notably, saruparib potently kills BRCA1-, BRCA2-, and PALB2-deficient cells at concentrations sufficient for near-maximal catalytic inhibition, without a corresponding increase in cytotoxicity in HR-proficient cells. Thus, saruparib combines potent HR-deficient-selective cytotoxicity with limited PARP1 trapping and associated toxicity. Consequently, saruparib closely recapitulates the PARP-BRCA synthetic lethality while sparing HR-proficient cells, providing a mechanistic framework for its rational clinical use.

papers.title: Loss of Notch signaling disrupts ventricular wall integrity and causes obstructive hydrocephalus
papers.abstract: Hydrocephalus is a common and severe neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by abnormal accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) within the ventricular system. Although its genetic basis is complex, recent studies have linked congenital hydrocephalus to defects in neural progenitor cell (NPC) maintenance, though how this results in ventricular obstruction remains unclear. Here we show that Notch signaling not only maintains NPCs within the ventricular zone (VZ) but also preserves the structural integrity of the developing ventricular system. Conditional ablation of the Notch effector Rbpj elicited premature differentiation of NPCs into neurons and disrupted VZ continuity. Cells lining the VZ lost their columnar organization, apical polarity, and adhesion contacts, breaking down the neuroepithelial layer and ependymal lining. This disruption obstructed CSF flow, causing hydrocephalus in neonatal mice. Pharmacological inhibition of Notch signaling in cortical spheroids similarly disrupted neural rosette formation, recapitulating aspects of the neuroepithelial defects observed in vivo. Collectively, our findings reveal critical roles for Notch signaling in preserving the walls of the ventricular system during brain development and provide insights into how disruptions to this pathway contribute to hydrocephalus.

papers.title: Epithelial network percolation reshapes collective mechanochemical dynamics and modes of competitive cell elimination
papers.abstract: Living tissues are active materials whose collective states depend on mechanochemical communication across connected cells. Yet tissues undergoing repair, ageing or tumorigenesis often contain intermingled cells with divergent states. How such heterogeneity alters tissue-scale communication, and whether cell competition can restore it, remains unclear. Here we track ERK activity, a dynamic readout and regulator of epithelial mechanochemical coupling, to ask how tissues recover from an aberrant state containing DNA-damaged cells. We show that damaged cells function as insulators, disrupting long-range ERK waves and partitioning control cells into disconnected clusters. As damaged cells are progressively eliminated by neighbouring control cells, fragmented clusters coalesce into a tissue-scale connected network through a percolation transition. Crossing this topological threshold restores collective ERK waves and coordinated cell motion, indicating recovery of tissue-scale mechanochemical order. Percolation also reshapes competitive elimination: before connectivity is restored, control cells remove damaged neighbours through actin-rich invasive protrusions; after percolation, connected control cells eliminate residual damaged cells by ERK-associated multicellular squeezing. Thus, cell competition actively reconfigures tissue topology to restore collective mechanochemical order.

papers.title: EFFECT OF A LACTOBACILLUS POSTBIOTIC ON DIGESTIVE HEALTH IN DOGS RAISED IN CONDITIONS AT RISK OF GIARDIA DUODENALIS INFECTION
papers.abstract: Giardia duodenalis infection is associated with diarrhea and dysbiosis in dogs, while metronidazole treatment can further disrupt the microbiota. We evaluated adjunctive LB fermentate HF (LBHF), a Lactobacillus-derived postbiotic, in a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled study of 30 naturally infected dogs (Terriers). Animals received metronidazole (50 mg/kg/day) with LBHF (50 mg/kg/day) or microcrystalline cellulose placebo (70 mg/kg/day) for 21 days. Clinical outcomes, fecal biomarkers, canine dysbiosis index, and cyst shedding were monitored over 45 days. Fecal shotgun metagenomics was performed at baseline and day 45. After baseline covariate adjustment, LBHF was associated with significantly lower Giardia burdens during treatment, particularly at days 10 and 20, improved fecal consistency, and reduced odor. No significant effects were found for fecal calprotectin, secretory IgA, blood biomarkers of digestive function, or canine dysbiosis index. Overall microbiome turnover was similar between groups, but multivariate analyses identified distinct treatment-associated community trajectories. LBHF was associated with increased Bacteroidota representation and functional capacity for plant polysaccharide degradation, alongside depletion of gene sets involved in flagellar assembly, quorum sensing, biofilm formation, and epithelial-cell signaling. Baseline microbiome composition also predicted Giardia burden, highlighting an association between parasite load and bacterial community structure. Adjunctive LBHF supplementation was associated with faster resolution of canine giardiasis, improved fecal quality, and coordinated microbiome remodeling. Further mechanistic studies are needed to establish whether the observed microbiome functional changes contribute to parasite clearance and recovery of intestinal health.

papers.title: The Neuroimmune Signature Underlying HPV Infection and Cervical Cancer Progression
papers.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer, yet the multicellular signalling programmes that accompany disease progression remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated Single cell RNA sequencing, independent microarray and bulk RNA-sequencing meta analyses, and TCGA CESC tumor data to characterize the neuroimmune transcriptional architecture of HPV associated cervical disease. Single cell profiling revealed progressive remodeling of epithelial, stromal, endothelial and immune compartments across HPV infection, high grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and cervical cancer. Although immune dysregulation predominated, lesion and tumor states showed coordinated enrichment of nervous system associated programs, including synapse organization, trans-synaptic signaling, axon development, neurogenesis and neurotransmitter-related signaling. These programs formed interconnected networks with cytokine production, leukocyte activation, chemotaxis, cell adhesion, apoptosis, and immune effector regulation. Cross-platform integration identified a recurrent 12-gene neuroimmune signature associated with tumor grade related transcriptional variation, including CXCL12, P2RY6, P2RX5 and TACR1. Ligand receptor inference further highlighted glutamatergic, adrenergic, noradrenergic, GABAergic and purinergic signaling circuits. Notably, these signals were distributed across immune, epithelial, stromal and endothelial populations rather than confined to a canonical neural cell compartment. P2RX5 showed the strongest association with advanced tumor grade, whereas P2RY6, P2RY11 and GABRP displayed cell type and stage dependent regulation. Together, our findings define cervical carcinogenesis as a distributed neuroimmune state in which HPV associated immune evasion converges with ectopic neurotransmission-related programs, revealing candidate biomarkers and potentially actionable signaling axes in the cervical tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Automated detection and classification of morphologically similar weevil species using AI for precision pest monitoring
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of morphologically similar insects is important for agricultural surveillance but remains challenging when large and balanced image datasets are limited. We developed Rostrum Recognition: A Weevil Identification Tool (RRWIT), a lightweight object-detection framework for distinguishing 14 weevil taxa, including two economically important weevil species, the boll weevil and pecan weevil, using more than 16,000 expert-verified annotated images. RRWIT was developed by transfer learning from a pretrained YOLO11n detector using a stratified data partition with the test set withheld from model and threshold selection. We evaluated this design with matched random-initialization and transfer-learning experiments, quantitative EigenGradCAM attribution analysis, targeted architectural modifications, and a frozen eight-framework benchmark across three independent training seeds. In the cross-framework benchmark, RRWIT achieved a mean average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.50 (mAP50) of 0.938 {+/-} 0.005 on held-out test partitions subset, whereas the newer lightweight YOLO26n achieved the highest value, 0.976 {+/-} 0.010, with a similarly compact computational footprint. Post-training 8-bit integer (INT8) quantization reduced the serialized RRWIT model from 10.09 to 2.91 MiB (71.2%) with a small validation mAP50 change from 0.978 to 0.971 but did not accelerate end-to-end inference under the tested central processing unit configuration. RRWIT therefore provides an extensible foundation for automated weevil identification while highlighting the importance of representative biological data, independent external validation, evolving lightweight architectures, and hardware-specific deployment optimization in future development. A publicly accessible RRWIT web application supporting image upload and live image capture for automated weevil detection and classification is available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/adamartukuli/RRWIT.

papers.title: Novel selective CDK4-inhibitor ALK-13743: Functional determinants of response in ER+ breast cancer models
papers.abstract: Background: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and CDK6 are central drivers of cell cycle progression in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, and pharmacological inhibition of this pair has become a standard-of-care therapeutic strategy. However, currently approved CDK4/6 inhibitors palbociclib, ribociclib, and abemaciclib carry associated toxicities, including myelosuppression and other adverse effects which are associated with inhibition of CDK6 that limits tolerability and combinatorial strategies. Here we describe the preclinical characterization of ALK-13743, a novel, highly selective CDK4 inhibitor. Methods: ALK-13743 was synthesized and characterized biochemically for CDK4 selectivity. Anti-proliferative activity was assessed in wild-type (WT), RB1-deleted and CDK6-overexpressing isogenic ER+ breast cancer cell lines (MCF7, T47D) using live-cell fluorescence imaging. Impact on cell cycle progression was evaluated by immunoblotting. Combinatorial activity was assessed across a 307-drug library. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in T47D xenograft models. Results: ALK-13743 potently inhibited CDK4/Cyclin D1 with an IC50 of 33 nM and displayed selectivity over CDK6/Cyclin D3 (IC50, 99 nM), CDK2/Cyclin E1 (IC50, 1854 nM), and CDK1/Cyclin B1 (IC50, >10000 nM) in biochemical kinase assays. In cellular models, ALK-13743 demonstrated potent antiproliferative activity in CDK4-dependent ER+ breast cancer cells at nanomolar concentrations, while exhibiting limited inhibition in CDK6-dependent cell lines. ALK-13743 exhibited single-agent growth suppression and drug synergy with the selective estrogen receptor degrader giredestrant and PI3K pathway inhibitors but was entirely RB-dependent and blunted by CDK6 overexpression. Single-agent ALK-13743 treatment led to tumor regression in T47D xenografts in vivo. Conclusions: ALK-13743 is a potent, CDK4-selective inhibitor dependent upon RB for its antiproliferative profile in ER+ breast cancer models. Its favorable combinability with multiple clinically relevant targeted agents supports further development, particularly in combination regimens, and positions it as a differentiated CDK4-selective therapy for ER+ breast cancer.

papers.title: SHMT1 and SHMT2 inhibition disrupts metabolic adaptation in glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma cells adapt to hypoxia and nutrient restriction through metabolic reprogramming. Serine hydroxymethyltransferases 1 and 2 (SHMT1, SHMT2) channel serine-derived one carbon units into folate metabolism, linking biosynthesis, respiration and redox defence. Its contribution to tumour metabolic homeostasis and adaptation to hypoxia and nutrient restriction remains unclear. We combined dual pharmacological SHMT inhibition using (+)-SHIN1 in glioblastoma cell lines, including patient-derived glioma stem-like models, with stable SHMT2 knockdown in LNT-229 cells. Functional analyses assessed clonogenic survival, invasion, migration and susceptibility to metabolic stress. Bioenergetics were measured by extracellular flux analysis and oxygen depletion, redox state by NADPH/NADP; assay, and molecular responses by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and 13C6-glucose tracing and tandem mass tag proteomics. Formate supplementation tested the contribution of limited one-carbon availability, three-dimensional co-cultures with human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived embryoid bodies assessed tumour expansion, and in silico analyses of public glioblastoma datasets examined SHMT expression, regional distribution and associations with hypoxia-related genes. SHMT2 was enriched in hypoxic and perinecrotic tumour regions and correlated with hypoxia-inducible factor-1 target genes. SHMT inhibition impaired clonogenic growth, reduced invasion and migration, limited tumour expansion in co-culture, and sensitised cells to death under combined hypoxia and glucose restriction. Under normoxia, it increased respiration and estimates of glycolytic and oxidative ATP production. In G55T2 cells, SHMT inhibition lowered intracellular and extracellular lactate and altered tricarboxylic acid cycle metabolite levels and 13C isotopologue signals. SHMT inhibition increased oxidative stress, reduced the NADPH/NADP; ratio in a cell line- and condition-dependent manner, and reduced extracellular formate accumulation. In G55T2 cells, SHMT inhibition led to a depletion of glutathione. Formate supplementation most prominently restored invasion and partially reversed other antitumour effects of SHMT inhibition, with the extent of rescue varying between cell lines. Under combined stress, SHMT inhibition attenuated hypoxia-inducible factor-1-alpha; accumulation, an effect counteracted by formate supplementation. These findings link SHMT-dependent one-carbon metabolism to redox homeostasis, invasive behaviour and survival under metabolic stress in glioblastoma. SHMT inhibition increases respiratory activity under normoxia while compromising tolerance to combined oxygen and glucose restriction, identifying metabolic adaptation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in glioblastoma.

papers.title: Cerulean Protein Tagging Enhances Immunogenicity and Osimertinib Response of Transplantable Murine EGFR Mutant Lung Cancer Cell Lines
papers.abstract: Lung cancers bearing mutations in epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFR) exhibit marked, but incomplete responses to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) like osimertinib. We previously developed genetically-engineered mouse models (GEMMs) for EGFR exon 19 deletion (del19) and L860R (mouse equivalent of L858R). Sequences encoding mC3 cerulean fluorescent protein were included to mark emergent tumor cells. Orthotopic implantation of mEGFRdel19 cell lines into syngeneic C57BL/6J mice yielded tumors that were eliminated upon osimertinib therapy which is not typically observed in patients while mEGFR-L860R cell lines failed to establish tumors. Herein, mEGFRdel19 and mEGFR-L860R cell lines formed tumors in non-induced mEGFRdel19 and mEGFR-L860R GEMMs and green fluorescent protein-transgenic mice, supporting mC3-derived epitopes as mediators of immunoelimination. CRISPR-Cas9 mediated disruption of the mC3 cerulean sequence in established mEGFR cell lines yielded two independent mC3-deleted cell lines that formed orthotopic tumors and exhibited partial osimertinib responses. These studies provide a cautionary tale regarding use of fluorescent proteins in murine cancer models and reinforce host immunity as a participant in anti-tumor TKI responses initiated. These mC3-deleted cell lines serve as improved models to explore mechanisms of incomplete TKI response, acquired resistance and cancer cell interaction with the host immune microenvironment.

papers.title: Subtype-specific autophagy profiles in Renal Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Autophagy is a highly conserved cellular mechanism essential for recycling intracellular components and providing energy and maintaining cellular homeostasis. The role of autophagy in cancer is double sided, where it can suppress tumorigenesis by degrading damaged organelles and preventing chronic inflammation while supporting survival of existing tumor cells to survive during starvation and stress, and thus support tumor growth. The role of autophagy in renal cell carcinoma (RCC), the most common type of kidney cancer, remains insufficiently described. RCC originates from epithelial cells of the renal tubule and is divided into histological subtypes where clear cell RCC is the most common followed by papillary and chromophobe RCC, showing differences in morphology and molecular features. Recent studies of RCC suggest that mTORC1 and autophagy are involved in kidney cancer development and response to treatment, advocating the need to better understand the role of autophagy in RCC. To this end, we investigated autophagy markers by immunostaining, immunoblotting and quantitative PCR in biobanked fresh-frozen tissue samples of RCC tumor and matched normal tissue. Overall, we found reduced levels of LC3B and GABARAPL1 in clear cell RCC, in stark contrast to chromophobe RCC and benign oncocytoma. This suggests that autophagy levels differ between renal tumor subtypes, indicating that autophagy could play subtype-specific roles. In addition, autophagy modulating drug assays demonstrated autophagy dependencies in metastatic RCC cell line spheroids. This could provide new inroads for therapeutical approaches in RCC.

papers.title: Immune Age Acceleration Stratifies Survival in Multiple Myeloma Independent of Chronological Age and Clinical Fitness
papers.abstract: Chronological age incompletely explains prognostic heterogeneity in multiple myeloma (MM), particularly among younger patients, whose clinical outcomes vary widely. Existing immune aging clocks are predominantly derived from peripheral blood expression data and thus incompletely reflect the aging of the bone marrow (BM) immune microenvironment in MM. To address this limitation, we developed BM immune aging clocks for ten immune and progenitor cell types trained on single-cell RNA-sequencing data from 1,260 healthy peripheral blood and BM samples and calibrated to BM. We then applied these clocks to BM single-cell profiles from 337 newly diagnosed MM patients enrolled in the CoMMpass study to derive a global immune age acceleration score. In patients younger than 70 at diagnosis, accelerated immune aging was independently associated with shorter overall survival (OS; HR = 2.24, p = 0.003) after adjustment for cytogenetic risk, transplant status, triplet therapy administration, chronological age, sex, performance status, and laboratory deficits, whereas chronological age was not predictive. Subsequent analyses identified CD4+ memory T cell aging as the strongest contributor to overall immune age acceleration and its association with shorter OS. Consistent with this, accelerated immune aging was characterized by terminal effector differentiation of memory T cells, TNF-/NF-{kappa}B-mediated inflammation, and increased lymphocyte-driven TNF, CCL3, and IFN-{gamma} signaling. However, inflammatory signaling alone did not account for survival differences. Longitudinally, changes in monocyte immune age acceleration at first progression were associated with shorter subsequent survival (HR = 3.06, p = 0.005). Together, these findings identify BM immune age acceleration as a prognostic measure of biological fitness in MM, distinct from chronological age and clinical frailty.

papers.title: The KMT2A-MENIN complex is a therapeutic vulnerability in SETBP1-mutant leukemia
papers.abstract: SET binding protein 1 (SETBP1) is recurrently mutated in high-risk myeloid malignancies, including myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative overlap disorders (MDS/MPNs) and is associated with poor clinical outcomes. Although SETBP1 mutations promote self-renewal and HOX-driven transcription in murine and cell line models, the epigenetic dependencies sustaining these programs in human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the KMT2A-MENIN complex as a targetable dependency in SETBP1-mutant leukemia. Expression of SETBP1D886N enhanced growth and serial replating of human HSPCs and established a transcriptionally permissive chromatin state, with increased H3K4me3, H3K27ac and KMT2A occupancy at SETBP1-regulated loci. Integrated transcriptional and chromatin profiling defined a 94-gene SETBP1 regulome containing HOXA9, MEIS1, MECOM, and MYBand was enriched for transcriptional programs associated with KMT2A-rearranged, NUP98-HOXA9, and NPM1-mutant leukemias. CRISPR-Cas9 disruption revealed a functional requirement for KMT2A, but not for KMT2B or DOT1L in SETBP1D886N HSPCs. Strikingly, deletion of the KMT2A cofactor MEN1 phenocopied KMT2A loss. Disruption of either KMT2A or MEN1 suppressed SETBP1-driven proliferation and leukemogenic transcriptional programs, including leukemia stem cell-associated signatures. We next exploited this dependency pharmacologically. A KMT2A-MENIN inhibitor suppressed canonical SETBP1 target genes and abolished mutant SETBP1-driven serial replating while promoting hematopoietic differentiation and reducing H3K4me3 at leukemogenic loci, despite modest effects on short-term proliferation. Most importantly, three clinically relevant KMT2A-MENIN interaction inhibitors impaired clonogenic growth across primary SETBP1-mutant leukemia patient samples, while inducing myeloid differentiation and suppressing SETBP1 target gene expression. Together, these findings identify the KMT2A-MENIN complex as a key therapeutic vulnerability in SETBP1-mutant leukemia. The consistent activity of multiple MENIN inhibitors across a variety of SETBP1-mutant patient samples and cell models validates the KMT2A-MENIN interaction as an actionable vulnerability and provides a strong rationale for expanding MENIN-directed therapies to SETBP1-mutant myeloid malignancies.

papers.title: Ex utero development of mouse embryos from fertilization to mid-gestation
papers.abstract: Early mammalian development has largely been studied as two periods divided by implantation: a pre implantation period, when the embryo transits freely through the maternal reproductive tract, and a post implantation period, when it develops within the uterine tissues. Although robust culture methods for mammalian pre-implantation or post-implantation embryos have been established, the continuous transition from the pre implantation zygote to organogenesis has remained recalcitrant to faithful capture in vitro in mammalian species. Here we establish PRE implantation Initiated Ex Utero culture (PRI ExUt), a sequential platform supporting continuous development of natural mouse embryos from the zygote to the E9.5 organogenesis stage, spanning nearly half of gestation without maternal interaction, embedding within exogenous extracellular matrices or co-culture with endometrial organoids. Cultured zygotes developed in vitro into blastocysts, formed egg cylinders, completed gastrulation, and progressed through neurulation, somitogenesis, axial turning and neural tube closure, generating embryonic and extra embryonic tissues with morphology and single-cell transcriptional identity highly similar to those of stage-matched natural embryos developed in utero. We harnessed this platform as a functional benchmark for mouse stem-cell-derived blastoids and found that supplementation with an in vitro-derived OCT4+GATA6+ primitive endoderm-like population substantially extended their developmental potential, enabling bona fide mouse blastoids to reach mid-gastrulation egg-cylinder stages, contingent upon application of PRI-ExUt approach. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that mouse embryos can self-organize faithfully from fertilization to mid-gestation independently of maternal input and establish a continuous experimental window into the first half of mouse embryogenesis. By supporting continuous ex utero development from the zygote to E9.5 in the mouse (corresponding to human Carnegie stages 12/13, 26 to 32 days post fertilization), this platform offers a flexible framework for evaluating the developmental potential of mouse pre implantation embryos and embryo models, and informs ongoing international ethical discussions and legislative efforts to revisit the limits placed on human embryo in vitro culture beyond day 14.

papers.title: Mechanical canalization of chiral gut morphogenesis
papers.abstract: Chiral organs such as the gut develop complex, stereotyped shapes, despite variability in the molecular and cellular processes that build them. How cell activity specifies tissue-scale handedness and reproducibly shapes whole organs remains unclear. Here, we use the embryonic Drosophila midgut to understand how a symmetric tubular organ reliably coils into a complex loop of alternating handedness, without any known left-right asymmetric gene expression.Through multi-view light-sheet imaging, 3D geometric analysis, and physical modeling, we show that midgut handedness is specified by epithelial cells in a neighboring organ, relayed across all three germ layers, and finally amplified and canalized by the mechanics of confined gut elongation. Myosin 1C expression in the hindgut epithelium controls midgut handedness up to hundreds of microns away, transmitting chiral bias to the midgut through migratory cells that form the longitudinal muscle. As the midgut elongates, a buckling instability then amplifies early left-right asymmetric constrictions, and confinement funnels the organ into a stereotyped coil. Tissue mechanics thus canalizes organ shape into one of two chiral forms, selected by an inter-organ cellular relay.

papers.title: A CITE-seq atlas of mouse embryonic hematopoiesis maps endothelial heterogeneity and reveals emerging HSC-associated states
papers.abstract: The emergence of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) from hemogenic endothelium during embryonic development is a tightly regulated process in which only a restricted population acquires molecular features associated with long-term hematopoietic potential. Although endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT) has been extensively characterized, the transcriptional and phenotypic heterogeneity accompanying the emergence of HSC-associated states remains incompletely understood. Here, we generated an integrated single-cell transcriptomic and surface-protein atlas of mouse embryonic hematopoiesis using CITE-seq across E9.5, E10.25 and E11.5 aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM) regions and E11.5 foetal liver. Analysis of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes distinguished arterial, venous, hemogenic and HSC-associated states, with HSC-associated signatures occupying a more restricted distribution than broader hematopoietic specification programmes. Hlf expression closely corresponded with HSC-associated transcriptional signatures and CD27 surface-protein abundance, identifying a potentially useful immunophenotypic feature for prospective enrichment of HSC-associated populations. Graph-based connectivity, diffusion pseudotime and RNA velocity analyses revealed heterogeneous relationships among endothelial and hemogenic populations, suggesting an inferred progression from arterial preHSC-HE through arterial HSC-HE towards more advanced HSC-associated states. Notably, analysis of E9.5 endothelial cells identified a restricted subset exhibiting elevated RNA velocity-derived connectivity towards arterial preHSC-HE. These cells displayed distinct transcriptional features with enrichment of pathways associated with cell adhesion, junctional organization and signalling. Differences in selected surface proteins further distinguished endothelial cells with high and low predicted connectivity. In parallel, analysis of arterial hemogenic populations revealed changes in transcriptional programmes and surface-protein expression along inferred developmental trajectories, highlighting coordinated molecular and immunophenotypic remodeling during HSC-associated development. Together, these findings provide a multimodal framework for resolving endothelial heterogeneity and identifying candidate cellular states associated with early HSC emergence. By linking transcriptional signatures to measurable surface phenotypes, this atlas offers experimentally testable strategies for investigating the developmental conditions that precede HSC-associated identity, while distinguishing computationally inferred trajectories from functionally established HSC fate.

papers.title: Breastfeeding Enables Systemic Transfer of Functional Maternal Immune Cells to Neonates
papers.abstract: Does breastfeeding transfer living maternal immune cells that persist and function in offspring, beyond providing soluble immune factors? Using a foster-nursing mouse model that eliminates prenatal exposure, this study directly tests whether maternal cells can be transferred postnatally through breastmilk. We found that intact maternal immune cells survive neonatal gastrointestinal transit, enter the circulation, and disseminate to peripheral organs. Single-cell RNA sequencing shows that transferred cells span multiple hematopoietic lineages, dominated by monocyte-derived macrophages with a distinct stress-adapted, inflammatory transcriptional state compatible with persistence in the neonatal environment. Interestingly, these maternal cells are detected at sites of neonatal tissue injury, consistent with chemotactic responsiveness. Our findings suggest that breastfeeding may serve as a postnatal route for maternal cellular transfer, potentially extending maternal immune influence beyond gestation.

papers.title: Activity-based fluorescence screening uncovers host enzymatic responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Transcriptomic and proteomic studies have characterized host responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet changes in endogenous enzymatic activities remain poorly understood. Here, we screened 89 enzyme-activatable fluorescence probes in living SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu-3 cells and identified 18 probes showing enhanced fluorescence, with some exhibiting multiplicity-of-infection-dependent responses. Neither SARS-CoV-2 Mpro nor PLpro activated the tested probes, and several did not exhibit comparable fluorescence enhancements in influenza-virus-infected cells. Target identification and biochemical validation implicated calpain-1 (CAPN1) and puromycin-sensitive aminopeptidase (PSA) as major contributors to probe activation. A PSA-reactive fluorescence probe confirmed that SARS-CoV-2-infected living cells showed enhanced PSA activity, which was suppressed by puromycin. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between PSA and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein signals. Notably, neither CAPN1 nor PSA was included among differentially expressed genes or proteins previously identified in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells. These findings highlight activity-based fluorescence screening as a complementary strategy to expression-based analyses for discovering infection-induced biomarker enzymes.

papers.title: New medium for the production of Dermacentor reticulatus and Ixodes persulcatus tick primary cell lines
papers.abstract: Background. The increasing prevalence of diseases caused by vector borne infections is an important public health problem. Currently, over 1000 extant tick species have been identified worldwide, and approximately ten percent of them are known to be vectors of pathogens (protozoa, bacteria, and viruses), leading to diseases in animals and humans. Tick cell lines are increasingly being used in research on tick physiology and the pathogens of vector borne infections. To obtain and maintain tick cell lines, traditionally used L-15-based nutrient media. However, obtaining a continuous tick cell line remains a complex and time consuming process. Therefore, it is important to develop new methods that can accelerate the process of obtaining tick cell cultures. Methods. To establish primary tick cell lines, we used, for the first time, a ready-made DMEM/F12 + GlutaMAX culture medium supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum. Results. In this study, it was shown that DMEM/F12 + GlutaMAX nutrient medium is suitable for obtaining primary cell cultures of two species of ticks from two different genera of the family Ixodidae. Primary cell lines of the tick Ixodes persulcatus were obtained for the first time. We also managed to accelerate the process of obtaining subcultures: the first subcultures were obtained within 1-2 months of tick tissue isolation. Conclusions. This new method, allows us to overcome several existing technical difficulties. It is likely that the DMEM/F12 + Glutamax medium can also be used to obtain and maintain tick cell lines of other species. Thus, an alternative to the traditionally used L-15-based media has emerged, allowing researchers to select the medium most suitable for their tasks. The rapid production of subcultures creates opportunities to conduct certain studies directly on primary cultures, without waiting for their transformation into an immortal culture.

papers.title: Tracking the trajectory of individual conjugative plasmids in bacterial communities using CRISPR acquisition-based recording
papers.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer mediated by conjugative plasmids is a primary driver of bacterial evolution and the spread of adaptive traits, including antibiotic resistance determinants. Tracking how these plasmids disseminate through complex microbial communities remains a major challenge. Current methodologies often yield static, endpoint snapshots of host identity, overlooking transient transfer events and plasmid encounters with the co-resident mobilome. To overcome these limitations, we introduce SPacer Integration (SPI) plasmids, which turn the mobile element itself into a recorder of its own transfer history. We engineered conjugative and mobilizable plasmids to carry a CRISPR-Cas adaptation cassette (cas1-cas2 and a minimal CRISPR array) and maintain tight repression of cas1-cas2 expression in the donor cell, so that upon transfer they capture spacers from the chromosome and plasmids of new hosts and store them permanently in their own array. Subsequent PCR amplification and sequencing of these expanded arrays provide a molecular record of both the bacterial hosts and the co-resident plasmids encountered. We created SPI plasmids using the backbones of well-characterized mobilizable and conjugative plasmids RSF1010, RP4, F, and R100-1. We tested SPI plasmids in defined laboratory matings and in complex wastewater communities. The analysis of the acquired spacers successfully mapped permissive host ranges and profiled the co-resident plasmids in situ. Requiring only standard cloning, PCR and sequencing, this accessible and cost-effective strategy establishes a new framework for studying plasmid ecology. Because spacers are integrated chronologically, it further offers the potential to reconstruct multi-step transfer trajectories across natural microbial networks.

papers.title: Modelling Maternal-to-Zygotic Transition Dynamics to Identify Common Gene Expression Baselines in Zebrafish Development.
papers.abstract: We propose a semi-mechanistic ODE-based transcription model for zebrafish embryogenesis that captures common baseline expression dynamics by integrating the maternal-to-zygotic transition mechanism. We fitted this model to a time-course RNA-seq dataset of D. rerio spanning early developmental stages until 120 hpf. Using the inferred model parameters, we identified common gene expression pattern using fuzzy c-means clustering and compared these with clusters stemming from a shape-based approach using smooth trajectories. We show that the ODE-parameter-based approach improves to biological interpretability by linking clusters to underlying regulatory mechanism, such as the timing of zygotic genome activation, thereby generating more precise expression clusters. However, the results also revealed technical biases of the time-course data, originating from the poly(A) enrichment step.

papers.title: An atlas of the sRNAs and their targets in Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is an opportunistic pathogen that causes various diseases in animals and humans. Small RNAs (sRNAs) control major steps in the infection process and acclimation responses, contributing to the architecture of the regulatory networks. However, a large number of putative sRNAs remain poorly characterized. Here we present aureoRNA, an interactive database (https://aurorna.biologie.uni-freiburg.de) that integrates available information for each sRNA, including phylogeny in the phylum Bacillota, public transcriptome datasets for sRNA and mRNA correlation, and permits computational predictions of sRNA functions. The aureoRNA-based analysis of the sRNA RsaD revealed new targets including the oxidative threonine catabolism and the arginine deiminase pathway. A target-centric search identifying potential sRNAs for mRNAs of interest revealed the citZ citrate synthase mRNA as an RsaE target, and two small prophage genes as RNAIII interaction partner. The aureoRNA database facilitates the functional characterization of the entire set of sRNAs and their targets in this major pathogen.

papers.title: TRAIT: A Toolbox for Rapid Assembly of Integration Templates for CRISPR/Cas- and Integrase-Mediated Genome Engineering
papers.abstract: The generation of genetically engineered mammalian cell models often requires repeated construction of integration donors that differ in their targeting sequences, genetic payloads, or integration strategies. Although modular DNA assembly methods facilitate construct generation, adapting existing expression cassettes to different genome-engineering applications remains labor-intensive. Here, we present TRAIT (Toolbox for Rapid Assembly of Integration Templates), a modular cloning framework that combines direct Golden Gate assembly of targeting elements with Gateway-mediated transfer of genetic payloads. The core vector architecture separates genome-targeting sequences from payload assembly, allowing existing Gateway-compatible constructs to be reused without modification of internal Type IIS restriction sites. We developed vector modules supporting homology-directed repair, homology-independent targeted integration, FrameSelect-compatible donor cleavage, coordinated guide RNA delivery, inducible Cas9 expression, Bxb1-mediated cassette exchange, and conditional transgene expression. An extended MultiSite Gateway workflow enables the assembly of complex integration donors using independently prepared regulatory modules, including components from the Mammalian ToolKit. Functional validation in human cells demonstrated targeted integration, recombinase-mediated cassette exchange, and multiplexed genome editing. We further applied TRAIT to generate human induced pluripotent stem cells carrying functional doxycycline-inducible Cas9 and candidate landing-pad integration constructs. Together, these results establish TRAIT as an interoperable framework for assembling and deploying diverse genome-engineering constructs in mammalian cells.

papers.title: Persistence of Non-industrial Gut Microbiota Discriminates Health and Disease States in Industrial Populations
papers.abstract: Industrialization has sharply reduced gut microbial diversity, possibly affecting human health. To isolate the effects of industrialization, we assembled 18,075 human metagenomes spanning hunter-gatherer, agro-pastoral, and industrial lifestyles. We confirmed individual-level diversity reductions in industrial populations, but also found that nearly all known human-associated microbes exhibit population-level persistence. Previously hypothesized 'vanishing' microbes are reduced from high prevalence in non-industrial populations to above-median prevalence in industrial populations. Species-level signatures in industrial case-control cohorts suggest that harboring 'vanishing' taxa can be associated with health or pathology, depending on the condition. Controlling for background prevalence, 'vanishing' microbes were more likely associated with cases than controls in obesity, both 'vanishing' microbes and those now 'blossoming' in industrialized populations were associated with glucose intolerance, while 'blossoming' taxa were associated with inflammatory bowel disease. We conclude that most microbes have not gone extinct under industrialization, and that the health effects of lifestyle-associated taxa are context-dependent.

papers.title: Persistence of commensal Escherichia coli strains and plasmid transfer in a healthy adult
papers.abstract: Little is known about the ecological dynamics of Escherichia coli strains in the healthy human intestinal tract. Here, the composition of commensal E. coli in a healthy adult was tracked over 700 days. 100 E. coli isolates recovered directly from each of 21 faecal samples collected at monthly intervals were characterised. In total 15 strains were recovered; five were resistant to one or more antibiotics. Five "persistent" strains were found in multiple samples spanning 1- to 5-month periods. The relative abundance of persistent strains ranged from 1-100% of E. coli per sample, but they were dominant (>80%) in 14/21 samples and the only strain in 12. Complete genomes were determined for all strains, including isolates of persistent strains from their first and last appearances. Persistent strains belonged to phylogroups B2 (ST1236 and ST420), A (ST10 and ST93), or D (ST362). Single-sample strains were phylogroup A, B1, B2, D or F. Confirming extended survival in the gut, only minor changes were detected in the chromosomes of persistent strains over their residence periods. However, one lost a plasmid and two gained plasmids, providing evidence for horizontal gene transfer in the gut. A Z-type multidrug resistance plasmid moved from one persistent strain to the next and exchanged a small backbone region with a plasmid in the recipient. An M-type arsenic resistance plasmid was acquired by two different strains and transferred to laboratory E. coli with two co-resident plasmids. All persistent strains, but only 2/10 single-sample strains, carried one or more plasmid-borne bacteriocin determinants.

papers.title: History of coadaptation to the cag pathogenicity island in Helicobacter pylori
papers.abstract: Most Helicobacter pylori strains use genes encoded on the cag pathogenicity island (cagPAI) to inject the CagA oncoprotein into human cells, where it alters cell signalling and morphology to promote bacterial colonization. However, cag- H. pylori strains are found worldwide. Here, we use a global sample of >9,000 Helicobacter genomes to investigate how strains adapt to cag status. We identified variants genome-wide associated with cagPAI presence, including many in vacA and hopQ, as well as in genes not previously linked to cag. We use these variants to construct a cag polygenic coadaptation score, allowing us to systematically explore the dynamics and evolutionary history of the island. Score distribution is bimodal in many populations, showing there is a stable adaptive strategy associated with cag- status. However, these cag- coadapted variants have historically been unavailable to strains in East Asia, providing a potential explanation for the low frequency of cag- strains in this region. We also infer that the cagPAI arrived in H. pylori before the human populations which colonized Australia and Papua New Guinea split from other groups 50,000-70,000 years ago. Adaptation to the island in other populations was achieved in part by using existing variants from the Hardy ecospecies. Our study illustrates how gene coadaptation shapes pathogen evolution after import of a major virulence factor and highlights genetic configurations that may predict increased or decreased disease risk, informing eradication strategies.

papers.title: Visual Search and ASD: Basic vs. Superordinate Category Search
papers.abstract: We study visual search and categorization among individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and a neuro-typical comparison group (NT). Individuals with ASD often exhibit distinct sensory processing patterns and may face challenges in efficiently detecting and categorizing visual stimuli. They may also process categories differently compared to NT groups, reflecting variations in typical sensory processing mechanisms. Based on our previous findings, this study employs visual search categorization tasks, testing reaction time and set-size slopes for different target categories. Participants included 26 individuals with ASD and 11 NT individuals, with similar mean ages and mean IQ Block Design subtest scores. They performed basic-level and superordinate-level visual search, as well as a categorization task. In the visual search task, participants identified targets within arrays of varying set sizes (4, 16, 36, 64). Face detection remained rapid across groups, and Basic-level search was similar in ASD and NT groups (mean set-size slopes: 48.7 and 45 ms/item, respectively). In contrast, superordinate search was much slower in ASD (99 ms/item) compared to NT (70.8 ms/item), reflecting increased cognitive demands. Object typicality influenced performance, with less typical items being slower to both categorize and detect. These findings suggest that basic-level processing is relatively preserved in ASD, whereas superordinate categorization imposes greater demands. The results highlight the role of typicality and support differences in perceptual and cognitive processing in ASD. Our findings contribute to better understanding visual cognition in autism and may inform strategies for improving conceptual generalization and visual learning.
